headline: Home Minister: IGP’s ‘crossfire’ remarks do not reflect govt position
summary: Salahuddin Ahmed clarifies that the government is firmly opposed to extrajudicial killings, contradicting the police chief's suggestion of 'crossfire' with permission.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the police chief's remarks about conducting 'crossfire' with government permission do not represent the government's position.
The Minister emphasized that the government is firmly opposed to extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and custodial deaths.
The controversy began when Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir suggested at a program in Dhaka's Chawkbazar that police would conduct crossfire if the government allowed it.

Police Headquarters and the Bangladesh Police Service Association later clarified that the IGP was referring to firm legal action against criminals and the right of private defense, not extrajudicial killings.
The Police Service Association defended the remarks as a 'timely call' for uncompromising law enforcement, noting that police personnel have faced 176 attacks this year.
Under Articles 31 and 32 of the Constitution, no person can be deprived of life except in accordance with the law, meaning the government has no authority to permit extrajudicial killings.
Bangladesh has a long history of 'crossfire' deaths, with Ain o Salish Kendra reporting 2,957 such killings between 2004 and September 2026.
The BNP's state reform program pledges to end extrajudicial killings and bring those responsible for deaths in the name of crossfire to justice.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Cyclone Arnab]] strengthens to very severe, heads for India's Andhra coast
headline: Cyclone Arnab strengthens to very severe, heads for India's Andhra coast
summary: The storm is packing wind speeds of up to 150km per hour and is expected to make landfall by Wednesday afternoon. Bangladesh's maritime ports are on alert.
details: Very severe cyclonic storm "Arnab" is moving towards the coast of India's Andhra Pradesh, with wind speeds reaching up to 150 kmph. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasts landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by Wednesday afternoon.

Bangladesh's maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra have been advised to hoist local cautionary signal No. 3 due to rough seas. The cyclone was located 1,130km south-west of Chittagong Port at noon on Tuesday.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay are warned to stay close to the coast and navigate with caution. The IMD predicts wind speeds of 125-135 kmph during landfall, with gusts up to 150 kmph, and a storm surge of 1.5-2.5 metres.

While the direct impact on Bangladesh is expected to be low, widespread rain and thundershowers are forecast across all eight divisions on Wednesday. Parts of Rangpur and Rajshahi divisions may see widespread rainfall from Thursday to Saturday.
